description: Authored development smoke suite, not a comprehensive language benchmark. No split is used for training model weights.
calibration: A clock coordinates the steps of a digital circuit. Registers remember values between clock edges.
To add two numbers, combine their quantities. Seven plus five is twelve.
A program reads its input and computes an output. Tests compare that output with an expected result.
An accelerator can execute many arithmetic operations in parallel. Data must also arrive quickly enough.
validation: The kettle contains water. Heating the water raises its temperature until it boils.
A queue stores requests in arrival order. A busy server may make later requests wait.
A triangle has three sides. A square has four equal sides and four right angles.
The function returns the sum of its arguments. For inputs three and four, the result is seven.
Memory holds information for later use. A cache keeps frequently needed information nearby.
The library opens in the morning. Readers can borrow books and return them later.
A measurement should include its units. Seconds measure time, while bytes measure stored data.
If a test fails, inspect the evidence. Changing the expected answer does not fix the underlying defect.
held-out: A bicycle has two wheels. Pedaling transfers energy through a chain to move the bicycle forward.
A compiler translates a program into instructions. The machine follows those instructions to produce results.
Latency measures how long one request takes. Throughput measures how much work finishes over time.
The garden needs sunlight and water. Healthy roots absorb nutrients from the soil.
A rectangle's area equals its width multiplied by its height. A width of six and height of three give eighteen.
An experiment changes one setting while keeping the others fixed. This helps identify the cause of a difference.
During a storm, the travelers took shelter indoors. They continued their journey when the weather improved.
A record contains both a result and its provenance. Reproducibility requires knowing which inputs and settings produced it.
